outcomes.accepted: The meaning and form are right. The quest moves on.
outcomes.accepted_with_correction: The meaning is clear but the form is off. Accept the answer, move the quest on and show the correction tip.
outcomes.not_accepted: The NPC reacts, then the quest's quick_hint appears as the tip.

answer_rules.accept_meaning: Accept the meaning, not exact words. 'Chaha beku' and 'Nanage chaha beku' are both right.

accept_any_spelling.rule: Accept any spelling. Common alternative spellings are listed as variants in vocabulary.json; the NLP part handles other spellings by rule.

english_mixed_in.rule: English mixed into a Kanglish answer is accepted when the answer contains a key Kannada word of the step (one of its target_words). An answer in English only is not accepted (english_only).

global_rules.rule: These apply to every step and need no entry in the quest files. An entry in a step takes priority over them.
global_rules.hindi_word: Hindi typed instead of Kannada, e.g. 'Chai chahiye'.

placeholders.{player_name}: Any name the player types. It is not matched strictly against Arun or Aditi.
placeholders.{item}: Any word listed in item_words (food and drink).

answer_rules.never_show_wrong: Never show 'Wrong'. The NPC reacts naturally, then one short tip appears.
answer_rules.tip: For a not accepted answer the tip is the quest's quick_hint. For an answer accepted with correction it is the tip of its correction_type.
answer_rules.default_reaction: If an answer is not accepted and has no reaction_id, the step's speaker uses r_puzzled — except Somanna, who uses r_somanna_ignores for English.

error_categories.description: Real Kannada, but not what this moment needs (e.g. 'Beku' instead of 'Dhanyavada').
Want and don't-want mixed up (e.g. 'Nanage chaha beda' when ordering).
Blunt form used with an elder (e.g. 'Bagilu tegi' instead of 'Svalpa bagilu tegeyiri').
Misunderstood what the NPC said (e.g. naming the wrong person in Quest 2.2).
Misunderstood a number (e.g. typing 'Hattu' when Shanthakka asks for 'aivattu').
Wrong pronoun, usually copied from the NPC's line (nimage/nimma) or naanu for nanage, e.g. 'Nimage chaha beku'.
Hindi typed instead of Kannada, e.g. 'Chai chahiye', 'Shukriya'.
Relevant but a required part is missing, e.g. 'Library' with no question word, 'Namaskara' with no name.
Good Kannada, but not the answer this step needs, e.g. refusing the meal with 'Illa, beda'.

correction_types.description: Meaning clear, the verb is missing (e.g. 'Nanage chaha').
correction_types.tip: Add the verb at the end, e.g. beku (want) or kodi (please give).
Say what to open: Svalpa bagilu tegeyiri.

correction_types.description: elli for a place or thing, or ellide for a person.
correction_types.tip: Places and things use ellide. People use elli.

correction_types.description: Question word placed before the place or thing (e.g. 'Ellide library?').
correction_types.tip: Say the place or thing first, then the question word.

correction_types.description: Beda where saaku (enough) is wanted. Keeps the reaction r_shanthakka_say_saaku.
Meaning accepted, but not the pattern this step teaches (e.g. 'Nanna hesaru {player_name}' in q2_1_a).

reactions.speaker: somanna
reactions.action: frowns and turns away until asked politely
